text:
sam: hey team, sam here (first day). trying to build the runtime from source in our recommended linux VM and running into a weird link/time-of-load error during the final link step. followed README and devcontainer defaults.
sam: link output snippet:
sam: ```
/usr/bin/ld: src/cuda/kernel_loader.o: relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against `__cudaRegisterFatBinary' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
sam: also saw earlier during compile: `ptxas fatal   : Value 'sm_86' is not supported by this toolchain` when building some kernels.
sam: nvcc --version: 12.1, host gcc: 12.2. Driver: 535.xx on the VM. I mounted /usr/local/cuda from host to container as per docs.
priya: welcome Sam! :wave: two things to try: 1) the relocation message usually means some object was built without -fPIC and you're linking into a shared object. Try `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON` or set `CXXFLAGS="-fPIC"` before cmake. 2) the ptxas message suggests nvcc/toolkit mismatch with arch flags. Set `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` (or the arch of your GPU) or use `cmake -D...=Auto` to let the toolchain pick PTX fallback.
chase: adding: for CUDA12 toolchains, gcc 12 sometimes emits code incompatible with nvcc wrappers; we pin to gcc-11 for CI. Try `sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/gcc gcc /usr/bin/gcc-11 100` and same for g++. Then `cmake -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc-11 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++-11 ..` and clean build.
priya: also check any static thirdparty libs you're linking. If a static lib was built without -fPIC, you'll get the relocation error. Run `file` on the .a / .o files in third_party to confirm. Rebuild those with PIC or prefer shared variants.
sam: run `file third_party/libfastkern.a` and it reported non-PIC objects. re-building that submodule with `CFLAGS=-fPIC` fixed it locally. thanks.
chase: for the ptxas issue, if you don't have the exact GPU locally, build with `-gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86,code=compute_86` or include `-arch=compute_86` flags aligned to the runtime GPU. Our CI builds include PTX fallback for older/newer GPUs; local builds can fail when host NVCC is different minor version.
dev-bot: dev-image-bot: note: our supported dev images are pinned to CUDA 12.1 + gcc-11. If you use the internal docker image `redwood/dev:cuda-12.1-gcc11`, you avoid many of these host toolchain mismatches.
infra-bot: infra-bot: if you need a ready dev VM with matching stack, request `gpu-dev-onboard` in #eng-infra and include your username and preferred CUDA version.
sam: helpful. i rebuilt the offending submodule with -fPIC and switched to gcc-11, link finished further but runtime fails complaining about `libcuda.so.1` unresolved when running in container.
priya: make sure the container has access to the host driver libs (nvidia-container-toolkit) and that `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` is visible. If using host mount, don't mount mismatched lib paths. Running `ldd build/runtime | grep cuda` should show resolved libs.
sam: `ldd` shows `libcuda.so.1 => not found` inside container. I enabled nvidia runtime for docker but still no luck.
chase: check `nvidia-smi` inside the container. If that's missing, the container runtime isn't configured. For local quickstart, use our docker dev image which has required hooks, or request infra to spin a pre-baked VM.
sam: ok i'll switch to the `redwood/dev` image and re-run. thanks for the fast answers, will ping if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
